metas.name: "KP" Consonant Cluster
metas.note: "KP" next to each other can be seen much more commonly in the Greater Accra and Volta provinces due to local language influence. Credits to seb010101 for this meta, which was posted in Lupus' Regionguessing Meta Library.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Accra Antenna
metas.note: Having an antenna in Ghana is extremely rare, but when it is there, it only appears in Accra.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Accra Houses
metas.note: Kind of a fake meta, but as a rule of thumb, most residential buildings in Accra look like this (light beige walls and triangle sheet metal roof) and almost none do in Kumasi, with about half of them looking like this in other major cities.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Asokwa Leaf
metas.note: This leaf above the tape appears north of Asokwa and on either side of Obuasi. Credits to amordys for showing me this meta, and thibeauvanuden for giving a more accurate distribution and making the attached image (which was published on Lupus' Regionguessing Meta Library).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Bar Ring
metas.note: A small ring in one of the roof racks of the car can be found in the general southwest of the country. Credits to thibeauvanuden for this meta, which was shared in Lupus' Regionguessing Meta Library.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Bimbila-Nkwanta Road
metas.note: The road going from Bimbila to Nkwanta has wooden poles to the northeast, and looks very dry but green. It is also unpaved.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Boabeng Car
metas.note: Most features of the car are missing in Boabeng and its reserve, which are disconnected from the rest of the coverage. The right mirror is still there though.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Bui Natpark Road
metas.note: The road to the east of Bui National Park has grainy pavement and is driving north or northwest.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Cape Coast Street Signs
metas.note: Street signs in Cape Coast are always green, say "CCMA" on them, and will show up at most intersections. Street signs in Kumasi will rarely also be green - they don't say "CCMA" but may be hard to distinguish from farther away.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Coastal Cape Coast Road
metas.note: This road in Cape Coast is the only somewhat rural coastal road driving east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ho Hills
metas.note: The town of Ho has prominent hills to the northwest.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Huni Valley Road
metas.note: This road near Huni Valley is unpaved and surrounded by palm trees and short palm-looking shrubs. It can drive any direction except south, but is usually driving north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Juaso-Nsawam Road
metas.note: The road from Nsawam to Juaso drives north or northwest, and is either badly paved or a dirt road. Travelling from Nsawam to New Abirem, the road shows increasingly worse condition before improving again as you get closer to Juaso.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Keta
metas.note: Keta is a town next to an inland lake - the lake will usually not be visible, but everything will feel very coastal with palm trees while also feeling quite dry and sandy at most parts.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Keta Lagoon
metas.note: The road in Keta Lagoon Protected Area drives southeast, is taken close to sunset, and most importantly looks very dry but still very green.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Koforidua Hills
metas.note: The city of Koforidua has prominent hills to the northeast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Kumasi Street Signs
metas.note: Kumasi can have several different colored street signs, which correspond to what part of the city you're in. Credits to torgeantihl for finding this meta and creating the image, which was published in Lupus' Regionguessing Meta Library.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Max West N1
metas.note: The westernmost part of the N1 looks very clean and freshly paved, and can either have no road lines or only center road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Mole Natpark Road
metas.note: The road in Mole National Park (which continues and keeps its appearance from Sawla to Fulfoso) has very grainy pavement, drives east (except a small south-driving section), and has deep orange soil on either side of the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: N2 Rifts
metas.note: Only the section of the N2 in the Oti and Northern regions will have rifts, while the sections in Volta and Greater Accra will not. (I didn't check rifts on every road, because some are so subtle that it feels like I'm making stuff up, so only use this to regionguess the road if you know you're on it)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Normal Car
metas.note: This is the car you will normally see in Ghana, which can be found nearly everywhere but less common in Ashanti and nearby provinces (the region Kumasi is in). This low quality image is the only one I have and I lost the json, but blue is the normal car (which can also be mostly blurred but always has a crisp edge).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Peeled Tape
metas.note: Peeled tape is more common in the north and east of the country. (Image from the Plonk It guide)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Phone Codes
metas.note: Ghanaian phone codes follow a general south-to-north pattern. Around 1/3 of the phone codes you see are actually useful - phone codes starting with 02 or 05 can be anywhere.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Region Names
metas.note: Ghanaian region names appear on many signs, and are especially useful for moving but have helped me before on NM and even NMPZ too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Salaga Road
metas.note: The road driving from Tamale to Salaga is perhaps the most recognizable in the entire country - it is very overcast and has extremely dark soil, which becomes darker the closer you get to Salaga.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Spotted Tape
metas.note: Tape with two white spots on it can be found northwest of Kumasi and around Mole National Park.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Car
metas.note: A car with a French flag on the front resembling Sri Lanka's Google car can be found in the general southwest of the country. This low quality picture is all I have and I lost the JSON, but red is Sri car (which can also include a fully blurred front).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Street Signs
metas.note: Blue street signs are most common in Accra, where they appear at nearly every intersection. However, blue street signs can also rarely appear in Kumasi or other towns. (There will also usually be a blue sticker on the poles for street signs in Accra - credits to seb010101 for this meta, which was published in Lupus' Regionguessing Meta Library.)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Tamale-Navrongo Road
metas.note: The road going from Tamale to Navrongo is very dry with only shrubs on either side of the road. This can be distinguished from other dry roads because the car is driving north (or west for one small section) and a handful of clouds are scattered throughout the sky.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Techiman Street Signs
metas.note: Street signs in Techiman are very common and always black. Black street signs can also rarely appear in Kumasi, however.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Unpeeled Tape
metas.note: Unpeeled tape is most common in the general south of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Wa Road
metas.note: This road goes north from Wa and circles back to meet it in the northeast of the city. It can easily be regionguessed by driving direction, which goes clockwise. It becomes unpaved around 1/4 of the way through, and can be distinguished from other dry roads because it has much oranger soil (and also either very wispy clouds or none at all, if you'd rather play the game that way).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: West Coast Road
metas.note: This road on the west coast of Ghana is the only west-driving, rural, coastal road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Yendi-Bimbila Road
metas.note: The road from Yendi to Bimbila is unpaved and very dry, with orange soil. It looks almost identical to south-driving parts of the Wa road but has more scattered clouds in the distance.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.
